questions.stem: An eventstream destination shows errors and no data arrives. The source sends CSV but the eventstream expects JSON. What do you fix?

options.text: Nothing; formats are detected automatically for every source
The data format set on the source to match what is actually sent

questions.explanation: Eventstreams read events in the format configured on the source. A mismatch makes events unreadable, and the runtime logs show the errors.

questions.stem: Where do you look for warnings and errors about an eventstream's sources and destinations?
questions.explanation: Runtime logs list warnings and errors for each source and destination node.

questions.stem: An eventstream's Event Hubs source stops receiving events after another application started reading the same event hub with the same consumer group. What should you do?

options.text: Delete and recreate the event hub with a new name and partitions
Turn off the eventstream's destinations, then turn them on again
Give the eventstream its own consumer group on the event hub

questions.explanation: Readers sharing a consumer group compete for the same partitions. A dedicated consumer group lets each reader receive every event.

questions.stem: You changed an eventstream's filter, but events still arrive unfiltered. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Filters only take effect on events that arrive after midnight UTC
The changes were made in edit mode and haven't been published
The destination ignores filters added after it was created
The lakehouse needs V-Order before filters are applied

questions.explanation: Changes made in the eventstream's edit mode take effect when you select Publish, which returns it to Live view.

questions.stem: An eventstream reads from an Azure Event Hubs source that has only two partitions. You set the event throughput level to High, but events still back up. What limits the throughput?

options.text: The eventstream retention, because events are kept for only one day by default and the backlog expires
The consumer group name, because it must match the eventstream name for the High level to take effect
The partition count, because with fewer than four partitions throughput is limited regardless of the throughput level
The destination type, because eventhouse destinations are limited to 1 MB/s of ingestion, whatever throughput level you choose

questions.explanation: When the Event Hubs partition count is below four, throughput is limited by the partition count whatever level you choose. Retention doesn't limit throughput.

questions.stem: An eventstream's eventhouse destination receives fewer events than expected. Which data insights metric counts output events that can't be converted to the expected output schema?
questions.explanation: Data conversion errors counts output events that can't be converted to the expected schema. Backlogged input events counts waiting events, and watermark delay measures lag.

questions.stem: Events reach an eventstream on time but arrive late in the destination. Which data insights metric is computed as the wall clock time minus the largest watermark?
questions.explanation: Watermark delay is the maximum watermark delay across partitions, computed as wall clock time minus the largest watermark, so it shows lag. The other metrics count errors or volume.

questions.stem: You open an eventstream node's Runtime logs to investigate a destination problem and want to see only the error entries. What do you do?

options.text: Filter the runtime logs by severity
Export the eventstream definition to Git
Change the event throughput level to Low

questions.explanation: Runtime logs have warning, error and information severity levels, and you can filter them by keyword, severity or type. The other actions don't filter logs.

questions.stem: After you raised an eventstream's event throughput level, an application that sends events to its custom endpoint starts having problems. What does the documentation say you might need to do?

options.text: Switch the destination from an eventhouse to a lakehouse
Lower the retention period to one day
Recreate the eventstream in a new workspace
Update the data client, because the partition count increases

questions.explanation: When you change the throughput setting, you might need to update the data client of custom endpoints because the partition count increases.

questions.stem: An eventstream destination node seems to drop events. Which two data insights metrics count errors in event processing? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
questions.explanation: Runtime errors counts errors related to event processing and Data conversion errors counts events that can't match the output schema. The others count volume, not errors.
